name: sum()
what_it_does: Calculates the total of the items in an iterable (a list, tuple, or similar) by adding them all together.
parameters: iterable - the numbers to add up. start (optional) - a value added to the total before summing, defaults to 0.
return_value: The sum of every item in iterable, plus start.
common_mistakes: sum() only works on numbers by default - sum(['a', 'b']) raises TypeError since strings aren't summed this way (use ''.join(...) instead). Forgetting that an empty list sums to 0, not an error.
when_to_use: Whenever you need a running total of a list of numbers, instead of writing a manual for loop with an accumulator variable.
